channel.title: siteupdown.com guides
channel.description: Plain-English guides to website outages, error codes, DNS, speed and uptime.

item.title: Online banking or a payment site not working? What to do safely
item.description: How to handle a bank, card or checkout page that will not load or errors mid-payment, without double paying or falling for scams.

item.title: How to test your internet speed properly (and read the results)
item.description: Why speed test results vary, how to get a fair reading, and what download, upload, latency and jitter mean for everyday use.

item.title: What is an IP address, and what does it tell people about you?
item.description: A plain explanation of IP addresses: public and private, IPv4 and IPv6, how websites see yours, what it reveals, and what it does not.

item.title: Why Netflix, YouTube or other streaming keeps buffering
item.description: How to tell whether buffering comes from the streaming service, your Wi-Fi, your internet plan or your device, with speeds needed for HD and 4K.

item.title: Instagram, WhatsApp, TikTok or Facebook not loading? How to tell what is wrong
item.description: A clear guide to social media outages: the difference between the app, the feed and messages failing, and what to try on your phone before you blame the service.

item.title: ChatGPT, Claude or another AI tool not working? What to check
item.description: Why AI chat tools slow down, error out or stop answering, how to tell an outage from a problem on your side, and what to do while you wait.

item.title: Why changes to your website are not showing up
item.description: The layers of caching between you and your visitors, how to find which one is holding an old version, and how to clear each safely.

item.title: Why a website may be blocked in your country, and how to tell
item.description: How to tell whether a site is blocked by your network, your country or the site itself, what the different errors suggest and what is reasonable to do.

item.title: How to choose reliable web hosting
item.description: What to look for in a web host if uptime matters: uptime promises, support, backups, location, scaling and the questions to ask before you sign up.

item.title: Wi-Fi keeps disconnecting: causes and fixes
item.description: Why a Wi-Fi connection drops again and again, how to tell whether the router, the device or the provider is at fault, and what to try in order.

item.title: How to set up uptime alerts without alert fatigue
item.description: Practical rules for monitoring alerts that people actually act on: what to check, how often, how many failures to wait for, and who to tell.

item.title: How to use a status page during an outage
item.description: What company status pages show, how to read the wording, what they leave out, and how to combine them with independent checks.

item.title: What is a load balancer, and why does it matter for uptime?
item.description: How load balancers share traffic between servers, how health checks keep broken servers out of rotation, and what to know when setting one up.

item.title: What is BGP, and why can one mistake take a whole company offline?
item.description: How the internet decides where to send traffic, what the Border Gateway Protocol does, and why a routing error can make big services unreachable for hours.

item.title: ERR_TOO_MANY_REDIRECTS: how to fix a redirect loop
item.description: What a redirect loop is, why browsers show "too many redirects" or "redirected you too many times", and how visitors and site owners can fix it.

item.title: What is a DDoS attack, and how does it take a website down?
item.description: A plain-English explanation of distributed denial-of-service attacks: how they work, why they cause outages, how sites defend themselves and what you can do as a visitor.

item.title: Website and network terms explained: a plain-English glossary
item.description: Short, clear definitions of the terms you meet when a website or connection misbehaves, from DNS and latency to CDNs and TLS.

item.title: Email not arriving or not sending? A checklist for site owners
item.description: How email delivery depends on DNS records such as MX, SPF and DKIM, and a step-by-step checklist for finding out why messages are missing.

item.title: Online game or app not working? How to tell if it is down
item.description: A practical guide for gamers and app users to work out whether a game server is down, whether lag is your connection, and what to try first.

item.title: How HTTPS and SSL certificates work
item.description: What the padlock really means, how certificates are issued and checked, why they expire, and how to avoid a certificate outage.

item.title: Why a VPN can break websites, and how to fix it
item.description: How VPNs change where your traffic comes from, why some sites block them or load slowly, and a checklist for fixing problems.

item.title: How to change your DNS server on a computer, phone or router
item.description: Step-by-step instructions for switching to a public DNS resolver on Windows, Mac, iPhone, Android and your home router, and how to undo it.

item.title: How to write an outage update that people will trust
item.description: A practical guide for site owners on what to say when your site or service is down, with templates and the mistakes to avoid.

item.title: A website works on one browser or device but not another
item.description: Why a site can load on one browser, phone or network but fail on another, and a quick way to find the cause: cache, extensions, VPNs, DNS and more.

item.title: How websites stay up: redundancy, failover and backups
item.description: The ideas behind reliable websites, including redundancy, load balancing, failover, backups and testing, explained without jargon.

item.title: How to read a traceroute
item.description: What a traceroute shows, how to read the hops and times, why stars are not always a problem, and how to use the results when talking to support.

item.title: Latency, packet loss and jitter explained
item.description: What ping, packet loss and jitter mean, why they matter for games and video calls even when speed is fine, and how to test for them.

item.title: Is it my Wi-Fi, my router or my internet provider?
item.description: A simple method to tell whether an internet problem lives in your Wi-Fi, your router, your provider or the website you are visiting.

item.title: Why is my internet slow? A step-by-step way to find out
item.description: Work out whether slow internet is your Wi-Fi, your router, your provider or the website, with a short series of tests that each rule something out.

item.title: Major internet outages and what caused them
item.description: Real examples of large outages, including Facebook in 2021, AWS in 2025 and Cloudflare in 2025, and the lessons that repeat from one to the next.

item.title: What is a CDN, and why do outages spread so widely?
item.description: How content delivery networks work, why so many sites depend on a few providers, and what that means when one of them has a bad day.

item.title: What is DNS, and why does it fail?
item.description: A plain-English explanation of the Domain Name System, how lookups are cached, the common ways DNS breaks, and how to tell a DNS fault from a down website.

item.title: What happens when you open a website, step by step
item.description: From typing an address to seeing a page: how DNS, connections, encryption and servers fit together, and where each step can fail.

item.title: How to monitor your own website: what to check and how often
item.description: A practical guide for site owners: what to monitor, how often to check, how to avoid false alarms and what to do when an alert arrives.

item.title: What to do when an app or online service stops working
item.description: A calm checklist for when a popular app or service is not working: confirm whether it is an outage, avoid common mistakes, and know when to try again.

item.title: What is a good website response time?
item.description: What response time means, which numbers are good, average or slow, and what usually makes a site respond slowly. Written for site owners and curious visitors.

item.title: Why big websites go down: cloud, CDN and DNS failures
item.description: Even huge services have outages. The usual causes are configuration mistakes, overloaded servers, cloud and CDN failures and DNS problems. Here is how they work and why they spread.

item.title: How to tell if a website is down for everyone or just you
item.description: A simple four-step method to work out whether a site is down for everyone or only for you, using a checker, another network, another device and the site’s own status page.

item.title: Why some sites block automated checks, and what we say when that happens
item.description: Many big websites refuse requests from monitoring tools. Here is why, how it shows up as a 403, 429 or timeout, and how siteupdown.com avoids calling those sites down.

item.title: How to clear the cache and cookies for one website
item.description: Clearing the cache and cookies for a single site can fix pages that look broken, keep redirecting or refuse to log in. Steps for Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari.

item.title: A website works on mobile data but not on Wi-Fi: why and how to fix it
item.description: When a site loads on your phone’s data but not on your home or office Wi-Fi, the problem is almost always your network. Here are the usual causes and fixes.

item.title: Fix “server not found” and DNS_PROBE_FINISHED_NXDOMAIN
item.description: What the DNS errors in Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari mean, and a step-by-step way to fix them on your device, your router or the website itself.

item.title: What does a 429 Too Many Requests error mean?
item.description: A 429 error means you, or the network you share, sent too many requests too quickly. Learn why it happens and how long to wait.

item.title: What does a 403 Forbidden error mean?
item.description: A 403 means the website understood your request but refused it. Here are the common causes, from blocked networks and VPNs to permissions, and what you can try.

item.title: Why a website can be down for some people and not others
item.description: A site that loads for your friend but not for you: the real reasons, from DNS and CDN problems to regional outages, ISP faults, firewalls and blocked countries.

item.title: How siteupdown.com checks a website, and what the verdicts mean
item.description: How our website status checker works: the server check, the fifteen regional probes, and what Up, Down, Timeout and Inconclusive each mean.

item.title: How to speed up your website: the checks that matter most
item.description: Practical ways to make a website load faster: server response time, caching, compression, image size and fewer requests, and how to measure each one.

item.title: What happens when a domain name expires?
item.description: What happens to a website and its email when a domain registration expires: the grace period, the redemption period, and how to avoid losing your domain.

item.title: Uptime percentages explained: what 99.9% really means
item.description: What 99%, 99.9% and 99.99% uptime mean in real downtime per month and per year, and how to read uptime numbers on a status page or a hosting plan.

item.title: What is DNS propagation, and why does a change take time?
item.description: DNS propagation explained: why a website move or DNS change can take hours to show everywhere, what TTL is, and how to check where your change has reached.

item.title: SSL certificate errors explained: what they mean and how to fix them
item.description: Why browsers warn that a connection is not private, what common SSL certificate errors mean, and how a site owner can fix an expired or mismatched certificate.

item.title: How to flush your DNS cache on Windows, Mac and Linux
item.description: Clearing your DNS cache fixes sites that will not load after a move or an outage. Step-by-step commands for Windows, macOS, Linux, plus browsers.

item.title: How to fix ERR_CONNECTION_TIMED_OUT
item.description: ERR_CONNECTION_TIMED_OUT means your browser waited and the site never answered. Learn the common causes and the fixes to try, in order.

item.title: Website not loading? A step-by-step checklist
item.description: A website will not load: is it down for everyone or just you? Work through this checklist to find out and fix the problem on your side.

item.title: 500, 502, 503 and 504 errors: what server errors mean
item.description: Server errors in the 5xx family mean the site itself is struggling. Learn the difference between 500, 502, 503 and 504 and what to try as a visitor or an owner.

item.title: What does a 404 Not Found error mean, and how do you fix it?
item.description: A 404 means the server is working but the page is not there. Learn the common causes, what visitors can try, and how site owners should handle missing pages.

item.title: HTTP status codes explained: what 200, 301, 404 and 503 mean
item.description: A plain-English guide to HTTP status codes: the 2xx, 3xx, 4xx and 5xx families, the common ones, and what each means for a visitor or a site owner.
